science_card_focus: Preserve the mathematically verified full-domain lambda_1,lambda_2 in [.2,.67]^2 and exactly two branch claims for eta=0 and eta=.1. Use the paper general equation at source line 402 for BOTH claims without algebraic simplification: each AST must be max(zero, subtract(log(lambda0), multiply(two_pi, eta_branch))), where lambda0=lambda_2*(1+sqrt(1-lambda_1^2))/(lambda_1*(1+sqrt(1-lambda_2^2))). Create separate source-anchored mechanism parameters eta_zero=0.0 and eta_point_one=0.1; eta_zero must not reuse the max-bound parameter zero. Keep private fixed conditions eta_zero and eta_point_one, public controls only lambda_1 and lambda_2, common readout lyapunov_exponent, and source_ambiguities empty. Remove localized_phase_lambda1_lt_lambda2 and initial-state branch conditions. Use square_exponent=2 and sqrt_exponent=.5 anchored to lines95-104; remove line361 opposite-sign dual-exponent anchor. No extra claims, domains, quantities, or source facts.

issues.detail: Both claims expose the Cartesian square lambda_1,lambda_2 in [0.2,0.67] but also cite localized_phase_lambda1_lt_lambda2 and say they apply only in the localized phase. The declared square includes lambda_1>=lambda_2. More importantly, for eta=0.1 the condition lambda_1<lambda_2 does not define the localized phase: localization requires log(lambda_0)>2*pi*0.1. For example, (lambda_1,lambda_2)=(0.4,0.5) satisfies lambda_1<lambda_2 but the source formula returns L=0 because log(lambda_0)=0.249841<0.628319. Retain the full source-supported square and max ASTs, but remove localized_phase_lambda1_lt_lambda2 from both claims and from the selected fixed conditions; reword the claims as phase-spanning Lyapunov predictions whose positive versus zero output identifies localization versus delocalization.

The intended hidden-world discriminator is eta=0 versus eta=0.1, but no fixed condition encodes either value. initial_state_hermitian and initial_state_nonhermitian contain the same state vector and do not define eta; using them as the mandatory branch-private conditions would misstate what differs between worlds. Add eta_zero, anchored to the source definition of the Hermitian regime, and eta_point_one_condition, anchored to the eta=0.1 phase diagram, and cite exactly one from each claim. The theoretical Lyapunov formula is independent of the prepared photon state, so omit the two initial-state conditions from this cluster or unify them only if experimental provenance is intentionally retained. Keep eta conditions private and expose only lambda_1, lambda_2, and L.

The ASTs correctly form sqrt(1-lambda_i^2), but the parameter named two is documented and anchored only as the 2 in 2*pi, while the parameter named half is documented and anchored only as the 1/2 in Phi=(sqrt(5)-1)/2. In the executable programs they are actually the square exponent 2 and square-root exponent 1/2 in lambda_1'=sqrt(1-lambda_1^2) and lambda_2'=sqrt(1-lambda_2^2). Thus the numeric leaves are reachable but their scientific provenance is unrelated to their AST use. Rename or re-role them as square_exponent and square_root_exponent and anchor both to lines 95 and 104; also extend the one parameter provenance to the 1-lambda_i^2 definitions. Keep two_pi as the separate source-anchored 2*pi coefficient.

The assessment usefully discloses the PT-threshold inconsistency and selects the internally consistent original-model equation at line 402. Nevertheless, lyapunov_eta_zero cites line 361, which is the dual exponent L^sharp=max(0,-log(lambda_0)), not the original UAMO exponent max(0,log(lambda_0)); it is an opposite-sign quantity and must not support this claim. Remove that anchor and rely on lines 108-111 for eta=0 plus line 402 for the phase-spanning original-model formula. Also make the inconsistency note precise: not only the main text but supplementary prose at lines 366-367 omits the 2*pi normalization, whereas Eqs. at lines 359 and 402 together with the reported 0.119 value are mutually consistent. Do not propagate the erroneous threshold wording into any selected parameter or claim.

previous_science_card.assessment: The source packet provides a complete experimental and theoretical description of the unitary almost-Mathieu operator (UAMO) and its non-Hermitian extension (PUAMO) realized via single-photon quantum walks. The selected quantitative cluster focuses on the Lyapunov exponent L_lambda1_lambda2_eta of the PUAMO in the localized phase (lambda_1 < lambda_2), which is given by L = max(0, log(lambda_0) - 2*pi*|eta|) with lambda_0 = lambda_2*(1+lambda_1')/(lambda_1*(1+lambda_2')). Two claims are built for the private regimes eta=0 and eta=0.1, sharing public controls lambda_1 and lambda_2 in [0.2,0.67] and the common readout lyapunov_exponent. The source reports the full parameter-space phase scans for the Hermitian (eta=0) and non-Hermitian (eta=0.1) cases, and the Lyapunov formula is explicitly given in the supplementary material. The extraction captures the central quantitative relation with all structural constants as named, anchored parameters. The source contains an internal inconsistency in the PT-threshold wording (main text states eta_PT = -log(lambda_0) while the supplementary and reported numeric value 0.119 for lambda_1=0.25, lambda_2=0.5 imply eta_PT = log(lambda_0)/(2*pi)), but this does not affect the selected Lyapunov equations, which are internally consistent. Therefore case_authoring_ready is set to true.

previous_science_card.paper_scope: The paper reports the first experimental realization of the unitary almost-Mathieu operator (UAMO) and its non-Hermitian extension (PUAMO) using single-photon quantum walks. It observes metal-insulator transitions in the Hermitian limit, PT-symmetry-breaking transitions, and a novel spectral transition where all quasienergies become purely imaginary. The selected quantitative cluster focuses on the Lyapunov exponent L_lambda1_lambda2_eta in the localized phase (lambda_1 < lambda_2), which quantifies the inverse localization length and is given by L = max(0, log(lambda_0) - 2*pi*|eta|) with lambda_0 = lambda_2*(1+lambda_1')/(lambda_1*(1+lambda_2')). Two claims are built for the private regimes eta=0 and eta=0.1, sharing public controls lambda_1 and lambda_2 in [0.2,0.67] and the common readout lyapunov_exponent.
